findings.reason: expressing the hold as a declared wait (status deferred, or a section dependency on sub-millisecond-forward-path §7) is what stops the queue and a coordinator dispatching from declarations from running §6 before the evidence it consumes exists.
findings.text: §6's new comment (line 216) states it is "Held, not dispatched" until run r-20261114T211231918544-polygon-tangent-repair reports the four rows, and that its node builds on that run's head only if the repair does not clear them; the section declaration at line 76 still reads data-status="implementable" with data-links="" and the plan's section-declarations meta lists "s6":"implementable", so the plan asserts the section is ready while its own content says it is waiting — a coordinator dispatching implementable sections, or the queue ordering on declared waits, has no record of the wait and can launch §6 concurrently with the repair it is meant to build on, duplicating the identity work and re-basing §2's identity reference twice.

response_events.note: The section now declares a link to sub-millisecond-forward-path section 7, the peer repair it waits on, so the wait is in the declared graph and not only in a comment.
